description.narrative:
In consultation with social partners and in line with international labour standards, the Government developed and validated a Gender Mainstreaming Strategy (GMS) in August 2022 during a stakeholders' meeting in August 2022, signalling the conclusion of the development and adoption of the Strategy for implementation as a means of ensuring that efforts geared towards improving governance and management of labour migration in Nigeria are gender responsive.
The Strategy complements normative provisions of the revised National Policy on Labour Migration (NPLM), detailing a clear-cut agenda for mainstreaming gender in a sustainable way in the labour migration discourse.
Towards ensuring policy coherence, the strategy takes into account provisions of other national policies and initiatives related to gender and the world of work, including the National Employment Policy (NEP) which makes provision for gender and equality in employment, the National Gender Policy (NGP) 2006 (as revised) which promotes gender equality as a development strategy and seeks to help women and men escape poverty and improve their standard of living, as well as relevant International Labour Standards.
The design and implementation of the GMS was facilitated through social dialogue, aimed at contributing to safeguarding the rights of migrant workers through the gender lens, particularly anchored on the major pillars of the Strategy which are: I. Discrimination, Exploitation and Abuse of Women Migrant Workers Prevented. II. Strengthened knowledge base and enforcement of gender equality and non-discrimination in migration governance and management; and III. Improved resource mobilization, coordination, and partnership for sustainable prevention of discrimination and abuse of women migrant workers. With support from the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the ILO supported the development of a Gender Mainstreaming Strategy (GMS) for labour migration in Nigeria. The ILO organized consultations and workshops for government, social partners, and other stakeholders, as well as technical backstopping services from its gender focal point. Additional technical expertise has been provided by the ILO to the Government to identify Gender Focal Points across the Centres that serve as the institutional mechanism through which implementation and sustainability of the Strategy is guaranteed.

description.narrative: Through social dialogue and in consultation with stakeholders, including employers’ and workers’ representatives and members of the Technical Working Committee of the National Policy on Labour Migration, the Government developed training manuals for delivering Pre-Departure Orientation Seminars (PDOS) to migrant workers. The process of developing the manuals was initiated and led by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment (FMLE) and validated during a stakeholders’ workshop convened by the FMLE in Abuja in August 2022. Training of Trainers (ToTs) in Abuja, Lagos and Edo states where Migrant Resource Centres (MRCs) are located were completed. The process of developing the manuals in addition to ToTs ensures availability of strengthened capacity in the centres to deliver services that encompasses information, training, and support in a gender-responsive manner for potential and return migrant workers. According to the normative provisions of the pre-departure manuals, seminars have been delivered by the FMLE, jointly observed by constituent representatives, while the Government continues to ensure adequate safeguard mechanisms in line with the National Policy on Labour Migration. The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) developed a Migrant Recruitment Advisor (MRA), a recruitment and employment review platform offering easy access to information about recruitment agencies and workers’ rights. Capacities of NLC affiliates to use the MRA in complementarity with the Trade Union Information Guide for Returning Migrant Workers were built and the country adaptation of the media toolkit for reporting forced labour and fair recruitment have been conducted. The recruitment advisor signals a new service introduced by the workers representatives in the area of contributing to protecting and promoting the rights of all migrant workers through the migration cycle, especially during the recruitment stages, with additional trainings rolled out to Northwest of the country. With support from the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, ILO supported the Government to develop manuals for delivering Pre-departure Orientation Seminars. The development of these manuals, in addition to further support provided through the Programme across the Migrant Resource Centres signals the introduction of new, inclusive, non-discriminatory, and gender-responsive services targeting improvements in decent work for migrant workers, particularly through sustainable institutional capacities. The manuals are aligned to International Labour Standards and take into account provisions of the national labour laws, and fundamentals principles and rights at work of all workers, including migrant workers. The ILO has trained 45 personnel of the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment across the indicated three locations through the Programme to deliver these services directly to beneficiaries who visit the MRCs. . The ILO also trained NLC affiliates to use the MRA effectively.
